videos.title: The Quantile Trick
videos.description: When you're doing a regression you're sometimes not so much interested in predicting the most "likely" value, sometimes you're more interested in predicting a spectrum of likely values. Put differently: you may be interested in predicting the quantiles of a distribution, instead of the median value. In this video we'll explain the quantile trick, which involves a pinball loss, to deal with these situations. videos.title: Physics Informed Machine Learning: High Level Overview of AI and ML in Science and Engineering
videos.description: This video describes how to incorporate physics into the machine learning process.  The process of machine learning is broken down into five stages: (1) formulating a problem to model, (2) collecting and curating training data to inform the model, (3) choosing an architecture with which to represent the model, (4) designing a loss function to assess the performance of the model, and (5) selecting and implementing an optimization algorithm to train the model. At each stage, we discuss how prior physical knowledge may be embedding into the process.    Physics informed machine learning is critical for many engineering applications, since many engineering systems are governed by physics and involve safety critical components.  It also makes it possible to learn more from sparse and noisy data sets.   This video was produced at the University of Washington, and we acknowledge funding support from the Boeing Company  %%% CHAPTERS %%% 00:00 Intro 03:53 What is Physics Informed Machine Learning? 06:41 Case Study: Encoding Pendulum Movement 09:19 The Five Stages of Machine Learning 16:09 A Principled Approach to Machine Learning 20:00 Physics Informed Problem Modeling 21:48 Physics Informed Data Curation 25:34 Physics Informed Architecture Design 28:59 Physics Informed Loss Functions 30:55 Physics Informed Optimization Algorithms 34:56 What This Course Will Cover 46:48 Outro

Why SQL?  Structured Query Language (SQL) is the cornerstone of data manipulation and retrieval in relational databases. Whether you're aspiring to become a Data Analyst, Database Administrator, or a Software Developer, SQL is an indispensable skill that will open doors to countless opportunities. Here's a sneak peek into our learning journey:  SQL Basics: Understand the backbone of SQL, including data types, basic syntax, and the structure of relational databases. You'll learn how to perform CRUD operations (Create, Read, Update, Delete) with ease.  Advanced Data Manipulation: Dive into more sophisticated SQL operations such as complex queries, joins, subqueries, and set operations. This section is designed to sharpen your skills in data manipulation and retrieval.  Data Definition & Control: Get to grips with creating and managing database schemas. Learn about indexes, constraints, triggers, and views, along with essential database administration tasks like backup and recovery.  Optimization Techniques: Discover how to optimize your SQL queries for improved performance. This crucial skill will help you write efficient, fast-executing queries, a highly valued ability in the tech industry.  Real-World Applications: Apply your knowledge to real-world scenarios. Comprehensive Coverage: From the basics to advanced topics, this tutorial offers an all-encompassing look at SQL. It's designed to be the only resource you'll need to move from a beginner to an intermediate level.  Real Interview Questions: The inclusion of genuine interview problems and their solutions makes this tutorial uniquely valuable. It's one thing to learn SQL, but another to apply it under the pressure of interview conditions. We've got you covered.  Expert Instruction: With years of experience in the industry, our instructor breaks down complex concepts into digestible, easy-to-understand segments. You're learning from someone who not only knows SQL inside out but also knows how to teach it effectively.  Interactive Learning: Engage with quizzes, exercises, and hands-on projects throughout the video. This interactive approach ensures you're not just passively watching but actively learning and applying SQL concepts.  Flexible Learning Pace: While the video is under 7 hours, you have the freedom to pause, rewind, and rewatch sections as needed. This flexibility allows you to learn at your own pace and ensure you fully grasp each concept before moving on.  Who Is This For?  This tutorial is designed for anyone with an interest in SQL, data analysis, or database management. Whether you're a complete beginner or someone with basic knowledge of SQL looking to advance your skills, this video will provide valuable insights and practical skills.  Getting the Most Out of This Tutorial  To maximize your learning experience, we recommend setting up a SQL environment on your computer to follow along with the examples and exercises. Conclusion  Embark on this comprehensive learning journey to unlock the full potential of SQL and propel your career to new heights. videos.title: Consistency Models
videos.description: In this talk, Dev discussed Consistency Models. In the words of the seminal paper on Consistency Models: "Diffusion models have significantly advanced the fields of image, audio, and video generation, but they depend on an iterative sampling process that causes slow generation. To overcome this limitation, we propose consistency models, a new family of models that generate high quality samples by directly mapping noise to data. They support fast one-step generation by design, while still allowing multi-step sampling to trade compute for sample quality."  In the session we focus on the details of consistency models, and how when trained properly they can outperform existing distillation techniques for image generation.  We started this by taking a look at Consistency Model architecture.  By using this architecture, Consistency Models achieve state of the art scores in generating CIFAR-10 and ImageNet images.  As usual, we had a lively discussion about the details and inner working of these models!   *Links* Our Meetup: https://www.meetup.com/East-Bay-Tri-Valley-Machine-Learning-Meetup/ Consistency Models: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.01469 Yang Song - Diffusion and Score-Based Generative Models: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wMmqCMwuM2Q Yang Song, Simon Ermon - Generative Modeling by Estimating Gradient of Data Distribution: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.05600 Yang Song NIPS workshop: https://neurips.cc/virtual/2023/workshop/66539  *Content* 00:00 Intro 06:13 De-noising Score Matching 17:35 SDE training 24:43 Computing accuracy 48:13 Sampling 01:19:00 Results  ▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬ 😊About Us  West Coast Machine Learning is a channel dedicated to exploring the exciting world of machine learning! We walked a series of block diagrams showing how information flows through the model.  To make this concrete, we reviewed segments of code from implementations.
